div.head: Ger 16

ab.seg: [16[a]] And gif he smeawyrhtan hæfð, ðam he sceal to tolan fylstan: mylewerde, sutere, leodgotan ⁊ oðran wyrhtan —
[16[b]] ælc weorc sylf wisað, hwæt him to gebyreð; nis ænig man, þæt atellan mæge ða tol ealle, ðe man habban sceal.
And gif he smeawyrhtan hæfð . ðam he sceal to tolan fylstan . Mylewerde, Sutere . Leodgotan. 7 oðran wyrhtan.
Ælc weorc sylf wisað hwæt him to gebyreð . nis ænig man þæt atellan mæge ða tol ealle ðe man habban sceal .
And gif he smeawyrhtan hæfð, ðam he sceal to tolan fylstan—mylewerde, sutere, leodgotan and oðran wyrhtan.
Ælc weorc sylf wisað, hwæt him to gebyreð; nis ænig man, þæt atellan mæge ða tol ealle, ðe man habban sceal.
Und wenn er Feinarbeiter [Handwerker] hat, denen muss er zu Werkzeugen verhelfen, dem Müller, Schuster, Bleigiesser [Klempner] und anderen Arbeitern —
jede Arbeit zeigt [von] selbst, was für sie passt; niemand lebt, dass er herzählen könne die Werkzeuge alle, die man halten muss.
And if he has skilled workmen [craftsmen], he must help them to tools, the miller, the shoemaker, the lead-worker [plumber] and other workmen —
each task shows of itself what belongs to it; there is no one living who could recount all the tools that one must keep.
And if he has skilled artisans, he must supply tools to them, miller, shoe maker, plumber and other workers.
He must know himself what each type of work entails, [as] there is not any man who may recount all the tools a man must have.
And if he has skilled workmen, then he must provide them with tools—miller, shoemaker, plumber, and other laborers.
Each type of work demonstrates the tools most appropriate for it; there is no one who can list all the tools that a worker must have.

div.note: Liebermann's 16 is split here into two rows. K: a stray bracket removed. B's ‘mylewerde’ is unclear (n or u). Liebermann compares Gerefa 9.
Rabin’s 16 covers the rows 16[a], 16[b]; it is given here, in the first.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Handwerker. Die im Domesday vorkommenden nennt Ellis Introd. to Dom. I 92. Über die auf Herrschaftsgütern s. Leo Rect. 131; Andrews Manor 236. Nur Unfreie scheinen gemeint, da die Herrschaft ihnen das Handwerkzeug liefert

Cf. Gl Handwerker. Ellis Introd. to Dom. I 92 lists those occurring in Domesday. On those on lords' estates see Leo Rect. 131; Andrews Manor 236. Only unfree men seem to be meant, since the lordship supplies them with their tools
Besondere, im Ggs. zu den allgemeinen des Ackers und Hauses Rect 4, 3a
Special ones, in contrast to the general ones of field and house, Rect 4, 3a

‘Mühlknecht’ Kluge, ‘Mühlenbauer’ falsch Sk-Wi; das Wort beweist, dass die Mühle (s. d. Gl) dem Herrn gehört. Der Müller ist ursprünglich nur ihr Hüter; Köhne Gewerberechtl. im Sprichwort 31. Die Glossen: mol(end)inarius verraten das nicht.—Zum Mühlenzwang 1067—87 vgl. Davis Reg. Anglonorm. n. 48. 56

‘mill-servant’ Kluge, ‘millwright’ wrongly Sk-Wi; the word proves that the mill (see that word in Gl) belongs to the lord. The miller is originally only its keeper; Köhne Gewerberechtl. im Sprichwort 31. The glosses mol(end)inarius do not reveal this.—On mill-soke 1067—87 cf. Davis Reg. Anglonorm. n. 48. 56
‘plumber’ Sweet, ‘Bleigiesser’ Kluge; leod für lead auch bei Layamon. Vgl. Gl Blei(klempner)
‘plumber’ Sweet, ‘lead-caster’ Kluge; leod for lead also in Layamon. Cf. Gl Blei(klempner)

div.note: ‘þæt’ is a conjunction, with ellipsis of the pronoun after it (Pogatscher). Liebermann compares Gerefa 12 and 17 f.
